ModularCurvesPartII.summary: Neither library contains a modular curve in any form: Tau Ceti's Katz–Mazur roadmap (#81) has no Lean code at this baseline, and there are no generalised elliptic curves, Tate curves, Jacobians, Weil pairings or algebraic stacks, and ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes exists only as Mathlib's bare pro-étale definition. What exists is analytic and group-theoretic: Mathlib's Weierstrass ℘-function with g₂, g₃ and ℘'² = 4℘³ − g₂℘ − g₃, the discriminant Δ ≠ 0 and the SL₂(ℤ) transformation of Eisenstein series (the homothety case for the lattices ℤz + ℤ), congruence subgroups, cusps with finitely many orbits, q-expansions and their injectivity; Tau Ceti's stabiliser orders and local models at elliptic points, widths at every cusp, and a large analytic Hecke theory (T_n, diamond and degeneracy operators, q-expansion formulas, newforms, strong multiplicity one, Petersson adjoints). Two geometric inputs of R12.4 are already in Tau Ceti: connectedness of Spec is invariant under extension of an algebraically closed field (both directions, for affine schemes), and connected schemes with domain stalks are irreducible. Everything else — uniformisation, the algebraic/analytic comparison, compactified moduli, integral models, Hecke correspondences, cohomology, Ihara's lemma and A_f — is genuinely missing.

targets.target: Complex analytic manifold (compact Riemann surface) attached to a smooth projective Weierstrass curve over ℂ
targets.note: Mathlib has the group of nonsingular points of a Weierstrass curve over a field, but no topology, charts or complex-manifold structure on E(ℂ) and no analytification of schemes in either library (grep for analytification/GAGA is empty).

targets.target: Uniformisation ℂ/Λ ≅ E_Λ(ℂ) by z ↦ (℘(z), ℘'(z)), compatible with the origin and the group law
targets.note: Mathlib constructs ℘ and ℘' of a lattice, proves they are periodic, meromorphic, and that ℘ has a double pole exactly at lattice points; there is no map to the points of a Weierstrass curve, no bijectivity and no addition theorem.

targets.target: Converse Weierstrass construction: the curve y² = 4x³ − g₂x − g₃ of a lattice, with ℘'² = 4℘³ − g₂℘ − g₃ and nonvanishing discriminant
targets.note: The lattice invariants g₂ = 60G₄, g₃ = 140G₆ and the differential equation are proved for lattices spanned by an ℝ-independent pair (`PeriodPair`). Non-vanishing of the discriminant is known only in modular-form normalisation for the lattices ℤz + ℤ: Δ(z) = η(z)²⁴ ≠ 0 and Δ = (E₄³ − E₆²)/1728, not linked to `PeriodPair.g₂`, `g₃`. Missing: g₂³ − 27g₃² ≠ 0 for `PeriodPair`, the resulting `WeierstrassCurve ℂ`, and the statement that every elliptic curve over ℂ arises from a lattice (surjectivity of j on ℍ).

targets.target: Invariance under homothety: G_k(cΛ) = c⁻ᵏG_k(Λ), so the curve depends on Λ only up to scaling
targets.note: `PeriodPair` carries no scaling operation and no lemma relates G_k of homothetic period lattices; the file's own TODO says the lattice Eisenstein series is not yet linked to `ModularForm`. Mathlib does prove, in coordinates on ℍ, the special case the moduli map uses: the Eisenstein summands and series transform under SL(2, ℤ) by (cz + d)^k, i.e. G_k(Λ_{γz}) = (cz + d)^k·G_k(Λ_z) for Λ_z = ℤz + ℤ. Missing: homogeneity for general lattices and scalars, and the statement that the curve depends only on the homothety class. On the curve side Mathlib proves that curves with equal j over a separably closed field are isomorphic by a change of variables.

targets.target: Comparison of the algebraic invariant differential and periods with dz on ℂ/Λ
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) as a basis of the Kähler differentials of the function field over any field and proves (f + g)*ω = f*ω + g*ω for isogenies; there is no integration, period lattice or comparison with dz.

targets.target: Scheme-theoretic Weil pairing on E[N] and its comparison with the analytic formula on (1/N)Λ/Λ
targets.note: No Weil pairing exists in either library. Tau Ceti has only preparatory inputs for its divisor construction — n(T) − n(O) is principal at an n-torsion point, and divisor-evaluation lemmas — and proves #ker[n] = n² over an algebraically closed field with n invertible.

duplicates.note: Constructs the complex manifold of an elliptic curve, proves E(ℂ) ≅ ℂ/Λ and identifies invariant differentials and period lattices: the same uniformisation targets.
Its acceptance tests compute the Hodge line and invariant differential of a complex elliptic curve, overlapping the differential/period comparison here.

targets.target: Classification of full, Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N) level structures on ℂ/Λ_τ and the resulting moduli description of Γ(N)\ℍ, Γ₁(N)\ℍ, Γ₀(N)\ℍ with functorial action
targets.note: Mathlib defines the three congruence subgroups of SL(2,ℤ) and their action on ℍ, but neither library has level structures on elliptic curves (naive or Drinfeld) or any moduli interpretation of the orbit spaces; Tau Ceti's Katz–Mazur roadmap (#81) has no Lean code at this baseline.

targets.target: Identification of the ordered-basis determinant (Weil pairing) with the chosen primitive N-th root of unity
targets.note: Depends on a Weil pairing, which neither library has.

targets.target: Automorphisms at elliptic points and the fine/coarse distinction at small level
targets.note: Tau Ceti computes the SL(2,ℤ) stabiliser orders (4 at i, 6 at ρ, 2 elsewhere; `ellipticOrder` is the PSL(2,ℤ) order 2, 3, 1), proves point stabilisers of Fuchsian groups are finite cyclic with a generator acting on the tangent line by a primitive root of unity (`Subgroup.exists_isPrimitiveRoot_stabilizerDeriv`), proves −I ∈ Γ₁(N) iff N ∣ 2, and proves Aut(E) ≅ ℤ/2 when j ∉ {0, 1728}; Mathlib proves arithmetic subgroups act properly discontinuously. The matching of stabilisers with Aut(E, level structure), Aut(E) at j = 0 or 1728, torsion-freeness of Γ(N) and Γ₁(N), and any fine/coarse statement are absent.

targets.target: The analytic comparison map is an isomorphism of complex analytic spaces, not only a bijection on points
targets.note: Mathlib gives a charted-space structure only on quotients by free properly discontinuous actions (its TODO lists the manifold structure). Tau Ceti has the local inputs for charts at elliptic points: the disc modulo μ_m is a disc via u ↦ u^m, a stabiliser acts as a rotation in the disc coordinate, and the orbit map is a covering on the free locus. No complex structure on Γ\ℍ is assembled from them, and the algebraic curves have no analytification.

duplicates.note: Identifies the fibre of the GL₂ Shimura variety over ζ with Y(N,ζ) and its analytification with Γ(N)\ℍ, with Γ₁/Γ₀ fine/coarse comparisons: the same identification in adelic language.
Builds the coarse quotient Riemann surface with its elliptic-point charts, which is the analytic quotient R12.2 derives.

targets.target: Local parameter at each cusp and the cusp width
targets.note: Mathlib defines cusps as parabolic fixed points, proves finiteness of cusp orbits for arithmetic subgroups, the strict width at ∞ (with its values for Γ₀, Γ₁, Γ) and the parameter q = exp(2πiz/h). Tau Ceti adds the integer width at ∞ (`Subgroup.integerCuspWidth`) and, for a finite-index subgroup of SL(2, ℤ), a width and a vanishing order at every cusp orbit (`cuspTranslationOrbitWidth`, the classical width or twice it when −I is not in the group; the widths sum to the index). Missing: an intrinsic width at a cusp of a general arithmetic group, and q as a chart of a compactified quotient.

targets.target: Comparison of the analytic cusp width and parameter with the Tate parameter of the algebraic curve
targets.note: There is no Tate curve (analytic or formal) in either library.

targets.target: Identification of the compact analytic curve with the analytification of the algebraic compactification (PR81 Layer 10 or R13.4a), extending the affine isomorphism
targets.note: No compactified quotient Riemann surface X(Γ), no algebraic compactified modular curve and no analytification exist; Mathlib's relative normalization, the carrier PR81 Layer 10 uses for X_H, is present.

targets.target: Scheme-theoretic cusp locus of the coarse curve (not assumed reduced)
targets.note: No modular curve schemes exist to carry a cusp locus.

duplicates.note: Constructs the normalised cusp datum, its width w and the coordinate q = exp(2πiσ(z)/w) at every cusp: the analytic local-parameter target.
Compares the GL₂ minimal compactifications, cusp loci and Tate parameters through R13.4a/R13.4b.
Computes the cusps of X_H via the Tate parameter (KM 8.11) for prime N ≥ 5 diamond quotients, the class R12.3 reuses.

targets.target: Connectedness of the fixed-pairing analytic quotient Γ(N)\ℍ
targets.note: ℍ is contractible, hence connected, and every quotient of a connected space is connected, so the orbit space of any subgroup is connected by instance search. (The contractibility instance is anonymous; its name is Lean's generated one.) Nothing is stated for the modular quotient as a Riemann surface.

targets.target: (i) Invariance of geometric connectedness of the finite-type curve under the algebraically closed extension Q̄ → ℂ
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves both directions for affine schemes: Spec A connected over an algebraically closed field stays connected after any field extension (with no finite-type or reducedness hypothesis), and connectedness of Spec descends along injective ring maps, so Spec A is connected iff Spec(A ⊗ ℂ) is. This covers the affine curves Y(N,ζ). Mathlib defines geometric connectedness with base-change, fibre, composition and total-space results. Not stated: the invariance for the curve as a `GeometricallyConnected` morphism of schemes, or for non-affine curves.

targets.target: (ii) Analytic isomorphism of the complex twisted curve Y(ρ)_ℂ with its congruence quotient of ℍ
targets.note: Needs R12.2 and the twisted curve of PR81 §5C, neither of which exists.

targets.target: (iii) Transfer of analytic connectedness to the algebraic curve via the smooth affine curve comparison
targets.note: No analytification or algebraic/analytic connectedness comparison exists (ComplexComparisonPartII C4 is unbuilt).

targets.target: Geometric irreducibility from smoothness and connectedness
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves a locally noetherian connected scheme whose stalks are domains is irreducible. That smooth (regular) stalks are domains is not available (no IsRegularLocalRing → IsDomain in Mathlib), and the twisted-curve identification and determinant compatibility are absent.

duplicates.note: PR81 §5C owns the connected ⇒ irreducible leaf for smooth curves over an algebraically closed field and records statements (i)–(iii) of this layer, in substance, as its external connectedness contract.
Exports the algebraic-versus-analytic connectedness comparison for smooth affine complex curves required by PR81 §5C, which is item (iii) here.

targets.target: Weight-two cusp forms ≅ regular (holomorphic) differentials on the compact curve
targets.note: Cusp forms exist (Mathlib) and Tau Ceti has Weil differentials of an algebraic function field with dim_F Ω_F = 1 and a space of regular differentials of dimension the genus, but there is no compact modular curve, no differential forms on Riemann surfaces and no identification S₂(Γ) ≅ H⁰(X(Γ), Ω¹).

targets.target: Hodge bundle ω matched with the automorphy factor (cτ + d) on ℍ
targets.note: No Hodge bundle or line bundle on a modular curve exists. The automorphy factor appears in Mathlib's slash action and in the derivative d(gτ)/dτ = det g/(cτ + d)², which matches (cτ + d)² with dτ, not with a Hodge bundle.

targets.target: q-expansion of f(q) dq/q and scalar conventions
targets.note: The analytic q-expansion of a modular form and its injectivity are in Mathlib, and so is the scalar relation dq/q = (2πi/h)·dτ in derivative form (`logDeriv_qParam`); the differential f(q) dq/q itself is not formed.

targets.target: Pullback and trace along the basic isogeny correspondences compared with the arithmetic Hecke action
targets.note: Tau Ceti has T_n, diamond and degeneracy (V_d) operators on cusp forms with the divisor-sum q-expansion formula a_m(T_n f) = Σ_{d|(m,n)} χ(d)d^{k−1}a_{mn/d²}(f), and proves T_p ∘ V_d = V_d ∘ T_p; Mathlib has the analytic trace of forms between levels. The geometric side (pullback/trace along correspondences on a curve) is absent.

duplicates.note: States S₂(Γ) ≅ H⁰(X(Γ), Ω¹) on the compact analytic curve, the identification of weight-two cusp forms with holomorphic differentials.
Its acceptance test compares f(q)dq/q with the weight-two Hodge section, the same q-expansion check.
Constructs the Hodge bundle and proves agreement of geometric and analytic forms over ℂ, overlapping the Hodge-bundle/automorphy-factor identification.

targets.target: Compatibility of the analytic/algebraic comparison with changes of level, diamond operators and complex conjugation
targets.note: The comparison itself does not exist. On the analytic side Tau Ceti proves diamond operators commute with the level-raising maps.

targets.target: Fields of definition of the components and of the canonical rational cusp
targets.note: No modular curve schemes, cusps as sections or component analysis exist.

targets.target: Named theorem replacing #81's conditional geometric-connectedness supplier
targets.note: Depends on R12.4, whose transfer steps are absent.

duplicates.note: Proves compatibility of the GL₂ comparisons with the canonical-model condition, level maps and Hecke correspondences, overlapping the level/descent compatibilities.

targets.target: Generalised elliptic curves: proper flat curves with elliptic or Néron-polygon geometric fibres, group law on the smooth locus acting on the curve
targets.note: Mathlib's group of nonsingular points is defined for any Weierstrass curve over a field, so it covers the smooth locus of a nodal cubic, and Tau Ceti proves a Weierstrass model has at most one singular point; there are no relative curves, Néron polygons or group actions over a base.

targets.target: Néron n-gons, contraction/decontraction and the ampleness condition on level structures
targets.note: Nothing on polygons of projective lines or contraction exists in either library.

targets.target: Descent and compatibility with #81's elliptic-scheme object on the smooth locus
targets.note: Mathlib has the abstract stack (effective descent) condition for pseudofunctors, but #81's elliptic schemes and generalised elliptic curves do not exist.

duplicates.note: Proves the moduli-stack algebraicity results used for generalised elliptic curves, overlapping their stack-level treatment.

targets.target: Compactified full and Γ₁(N) moduli problems and the correct Γ₀(n) problem (Česnavičius' refinement with boundary data)
targets.note: No moduli problems of (generalised) elliptic curves with level structure exist in either library.

targets.note: Neither library has algebraic stacks or algebraic spaces (grep AlgebraicSpace/AlgebraicStack/DeligneMumford is empty); Mathlib has the abstract stack condition, relatively representable morphisms and a Zariski-local representability theorem for sheaves on schemes, but nothing is algebraic, proper or normal for stacks.

targets.note: #81's affine problems are not formalised.

targets.note: No Tate curve exists in either library, analytic or formal.

targets.target: Completed local rings at cusps, cusp widths and the Hodge line near the boundary
targets.note: Only analytic, group-theoretic cusp widths exist: Mathlib's width at ∞ and Tau Ceti's width of every cusp orbit of a finite-index subgroup of SL(2, ℤ). There are no formal neighbourhoods of cusps, completed local rings or Hodge line near the boundary.

targets.target: Formal comparison underlying the q-expansion principle
targets.note: Mathlib proves the analytic statement that a modular form is determined by its q-expansion; the algebraic q-expansion principle via the Tate curve is absent.

targets.target: Ramification and stabilisers at cusps including characteristics 2 and 3; finite-flat cusp fibre versus reduced locus and Cartier structure
targets.note: No cusp schemes or relative Cartier divisors exist (grep RelativeEffectiveCartier is empty). Tau Ceti has only absolute Cartier divisors on integral schemes.

duplicates.note: Constructs the Tate curve over a complete valued field, overlapping the Tate-curve construction (not its generalised-elliptic extension).
Compares the Tate curve, its invariant differential du/u, torsion and q under isogeny, restating part of the Tate-curve analysis.

targets.target: Combined interface of R13.4a and R13.4b
targets.note: The layer states no mathematics of its own: it is defined as the conjunction of R13.4a and R13.4b, both of which are unbuilt.

targets.target: Coarse compactified curves from the stack presentations via finite-inertia quotients and normalization, for full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level
targets.note: Mathlib has relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property, but no coarse spaces, stack quotients or modular curves.

targets.note: No compactified curves exist to carry these properties.

targets.target: Identification of affine opens with PR81 by the moduli universal property and agreement with PR81 Layer 10 for prime N ≥ 5 diamond quotients after inverting N
targets.note: PR81's curves are not formalised.

duplicates.note: Constructs X_H by normalising ℙ¹_j in Y_H for prime N ≥ 5 diamond quotients, the special case with which R13.4a must agree.
Proves existence of coarse spaces for finite-inertia quotient presentations with normalisation and base change, the general construction applied here.

targets.note: Neither the curves nor analytification exist.

targets.note: Only analytic maps exist: Tau Ceti's degeneracy maps V_d with T_p ∘ V_d = V_d ∘ T_p for p ∤ N, and Mathlib's trace of modular forms between levels.

Compares the generic-fibre toroidal/minimal curve for F = ℚ with R13.4a/R13.4b.

targets.note: No integral models of modular curves, supersingular loci or local models exist.

targets.target: Igusa components
targets.note: grep Igusa returns nothing in either library.

targets.note: Tau Ceti packages flat finite-presentation models over a DVR and the numerical types of regular models' special fibres, but has no resolution, regular or semistable models. targets.target: Hecke/degeneracy compatibility on bad fibres and inputs to nearby-cycle and character-group computations
targets.note: No nearby cycles or bad-fibre geometry; Mathlib's pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes is only a definition, with no degeneration theory.

targets.note: The operators exist only analytically on modular and cusp forms (Tau Ceti). Isogenies of elliptic curves exist over a field, but there are no families, moduli of cyclic subgroups or correspondences on curves.

targets.target: Extension to compactifications
targets.note: No compactified curves exist.

targets.target: Composition, double-coset and adjoint formulas
targets.note: Mathlib defines the abstract double-coset Hecke ring of a Hecke pair. Tau Ceti gives it its ring structure and commutativity from an anti-involution, proves the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring commutative (`commSemiringHeckeRingGamma0`) with its multiplication table T_m·T_n = Σ_{d ∣ (m,n)} d·S_d·T_{mn/d²}, and proves the Petersson adjoint of a slash, ⟪f∣α, h⟫ = ⟪f, h∣α^ι⟫. The operator identity T_n* = ⟨n⟩⁻¹T_n is not proved. All of this is group-theoretic or analytic, not relations among geometric correspondences.

Owns the analytic Hecke operators and double-coset formulas that the q-expansion comparison targets.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field, an Abel–Jacobi map into divisor class groups and the pullback (conorm) of divisor classes along a finite extension of function fields, but no norm on class groups, Jacobian variety, Picard scheme or modular curve.

targets.target: Hecke relations and polarisation (Rosati) adjointness on Jacobians
targets.note: No polarisations or Jacobians exist.

targets.target: Integral Hecke algebra via faithful action on a finite module, finite over the coefficient ring
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the ring homomorphism from the integral Γ₀(N) Hecke ring to End_ℂ(S_k(N, χ)), so a Hecke algebra over ℂ is implicit; there is no integral lattice or Jacobian for it to act on faithfully and no finiteness over ℤ (no declaration is named HeckeAlgebra; the word occurs only in comments).

targets.note: No Tate modules exist (grep TateModule is empty).

Nothing is computed for curves, there are no local systems on schemes, and no modular curves exist. Tau Ceti also has symmetric powers of representations, so Sym^{k−2} coefficients for group cohomology can be formed, but nothing is computed with them.

targets.note: No Hecke algebras or cohomology to localise.

targets.note: grep Ihara finds nothing in either library; no integral cohomology of modular curves exists. Only the analytic, characteristic-zero injectivity of the degeneracy maps V_d on cusp forms exists (Tau Ceti), which the layer says does not give integral saturation.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has bundled newforms (with eigenvalues at indices prime to the level) and abelian varieties over a field, but no Jacobians of modular curves or quotients of abelian varieties.

NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.summary: Neither library has Néron models, abelian schemes, formal schemes, Tate modules, Picard schemes, semistable reduction of abelian varieties, or conductors of abelian varieties, so every layer is unbuilt. The available ingredients are mostly equation-level and field-level: Mathlib's integral and minimal Weierstrass models over a DVR with good/multiplicative/additive reduction and the local L-polynomial of an elliptic curve; Tau Ceti's abelian varieties over a field with isogenies and tangent space, the formal-group description of the kernel of reduction E₁, invariance of the minimal discriminant, and identity components and finite étale component groups of finite-type affine groups over an algebraically closed field. Over a base, Mathlib has group schemes over any affine base and Tau Ceti has their closed subgroup schemes, isogenies with base change, and special fibres of schemes over a local ring. The one piece of genuine degeneration theory is Tau Ceti's combinatorics of numerical types: Pic(T) as the cokernel of the weighted intersection matrix with its rank, degree and torsion results, which is the combinatorial half of the R11.4 component-group description.

targets.target: Néron model of an abelian variety: smooth separated finite-type group scheme over a DVR or Dedekind base with the Néron mapping property
targets.note: Apart from one Néron–Severi remark, 'Néron' occurs only in the Néron–Tate height pairing. Mathlib has the smooth, separated and finite-type morphism classes and group schemes over any affine base (`hopfSpec`, group objects in `Over S`); Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field, closed subgroup schemes and isogenies of group schemes over an arbitrary base, and flat finite-presentation models of schemes over a DVR. There are no abelian schemes, no Néron models and no extension property.

targets.target: Local existence over excellent DVRs via weak Néron models and smoothening
targets.note: Neither excellence (`IsExcellent` occurs only in a Tau Ceti docstring recording its absence), dilatations/smoothening nor weak Néron models exist.

targets.target: Dedekind local-to-global construction over rings of integers and S-integers: extend over a dense open, glue the remaining local models, global mapping property and finite type
targets.note: S-integers of a Dedekind domain and gluing of schemes exist in Mathlib (Tau Ceti proves the S-integers have finite class group whenever the base ring does); there are no local models to glue. Mathlib can spread a morphism out from a stalk to an open neighbourhood (`spread_out_of_isGermInjective`), but not schemes, group laws or smoothness.

targets.target: Uniqueness of Néron models and functorial extension of homomorphisms
targets.note: Isogenies exist between abelian varieties over a field and, as finite flat surjective homomorphisms with base change, between group schemes over any affine base (Tau Ceti `GroupScheme.IsIsogeny`); nothing gives uniqueness of Néron models or extension of homomorphisms.

targets.target: Global invariant-differential lattice of the Néron model and its localisations
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Zariski tangent space at the identity of an abelian variety over a field, the invariant differential of a Weierstrass curve and the co-Lie module ker ε/(ker ε)² of an affine group scheme over any ring; no integral lattice of differentials over a ring of integers.

targets.target: Comparison of good reduction with the existence of an abelian-scheme model
targets.note: Mathlib's good reduction is an equation-level predicate on a minimal Weierstrass equation over a DVR; no abelian schemes or scheme-level comparison.

targets.target: Étale/unramified base-change compatibility of Néron models
targets.note: No Néron models to base change.

targets.target: Identity component and component group Φ of the special fibre of a Néron model
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the identity component and the finite étale component group of a finite-type affine group over an algebraically closed field, and the special fibre of any scheme over a local ring (`specialFiber`); special fibres of Néron models are generally not affine, and Néron models do not exist here.

targets.target: Toric and abelian parts (Chevalley decomposition) and the character group of the toric part
targets.note: No Chevalley structure theorem for connected commutative group schemes; character groups exist only for affine commutative Hopf algebras.

targets.target: Functoriality under isogeny and the exact sequences used in modular-curve arguments
targets.note: Isogenies exist for abelian varieties over a field and for group schemes over any affine base (Tau Ceti), but there is no functoriality of Néron component or character groups and none of the exact sequences.

targets.target: Rational component group Φ(k) distinguished from its geometric points
targets.note: No component groups of Néron models.

targets.target: For elliptic curves, comparison with the reduction filtration E₁ ⊂ E₀ ⊂ E and Tate's algorithm, including wild primes
targets.note: The equation-level ingredients are partly present — Mathlib's good/multiplicative/additive reduction classes and Tau Ceti's identification of the formal group Ê(𝔪) with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole (E₁) — but E₀, Tate's algorithm and Kodaira symbols (grep empty) and any Néron-model comparison are absent. Tau Ceti also has E₁ as a subgroup (`polePoints`), but only at places of a function field that are trivial on the constant field.

duplicates.note: Tate's algorithm there computes c_p = [E(K) : E₀(K)] and the component count, the equation-level side of the elliptic component-group comparison.
Constructs identity components and component groups of affine algebraic groups, the same constructions in the affine setting.

targets.target: Semistable reduction theorem for abelian varieties after a finite extension
targets.note: Nothing concerns semistable reduction of abelian varieties or semi-abelian schemes. Tau Ceti's StableReduction tree formalises preliminaries from the Stacks chapter on semistable reduction of curves (numerical types, models over a DVR, finite extensions of a DVR); the word 'semistable' itself occurs only in one docstring.

targets.target: Grothendieck's monodromy criterion relating semistability to unipotent inertia action on T_ℓ
targets.note: No Tate modules (grep TateModule empty) and no Galois representations of abelian varieties.

targets.target: Raynaud extension of the formal completion by a torus
targets.note: No formal schemes (grep FormalScheme empty) and no extensions of abelian schemes by tori.

targets.target: Uniformisation of degenerating abelian varieties/Jacobians with polarisation and lattice conditions
targets.note: No rigid or formal uniformisation; Tau Ceti's adic-space and Huber-ring foundations do not reach quotients by lattices.

duplicates.note: Proves nodal reduction of curves after finite extension and its equivalence with semistable reduction of the Jacobian, the curve case of this layer.

Constructs extensions of abelian schemes by tori and the polarised degeneration data with their algebraisation, which is the Raynaud extension and lattice uniformisation of degenerating abelian varieties stated here.

targets.target: Degree-zero Picard scheme / generalised Jacobian of a semistable curve
targets.note: No relative Picard functor, Picard scheme or generalised Jacobian (grep PicardScheme/PicardFunctor is empty). Mathlib has the Picard group of a commutative ring and its absolute functor on rings (`CommRing.Pic`, `CommRing.Pic.functor`); Tau Ceti has the monoid of line-bundle classes on a scheme (`LineBundleClass`, inverses not yet constructed), degree-zero divisor class groups of curves over a field and abelian varieties.

targets.target: Toric character group identified with H₁ of the dual graph
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the simple intersection graph of an abstract numerical type and its first Betti number; it forgets edge multiplicities (numbers of nodes) and is not linked to any torus.

targets.target: Grothendieck's monodromy pairing on character groups
targets.note: No character groups of Néron models.

targets.target: Component group described by the (weighted) intersection matrix under the exact regularity hypotheses
targets.note: The combinatorial side is in Tau Ceti: Pic(T) as the cokernel of the weighted intersection matrix of a numerical type (Stacks 0C7H), its injection into Coker(A), rank one, the degree map and the finite ℓ-torsion subgroups, which have degree zero. Missing: Pic⁰(T) as a named group, numerical types of actual regular models and the identification of the degree-zero torsion with the Néron component group.

targets.target: Relation of the Picard scheme of the special fibre to the Néron model of the Jacobian
targets.note: Neither object exists.

duplicates.note: Defines numerical types and Pic(T) and compares line bundles on regular models with it, the combinatorial component-group description used here.
Computes the dual graph and specialisation sequence of strictly semistable curves compatibly with their Jacobian/Tate-module description.

targets.target: ℓ-adic Tate modules of abelian varieties with Galois action
targets.note: grep TateModule/Tate module finds nothing in either library; Mathlib defines pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology Hⁱ(X, ℤ_ℓ) of schemes but proves nothing about it beyond the empty scheme, and there is no Galois action.

targets.target: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion (good reduction ⇔ unramified T_ℓ)
targets.note: No criterion, even for elliptic curves; only the equation-level good-reduction predicate exists.

targets.target: Good and semistable p-adic comparisons (crystalline/semistable Tate modules) via R06
targets.note: No p-adic Hodge theory of Galois representations in either library: Mathlib has the de Rham period rings B_dR⁺ and B_dR with Fontaine's θ, but no crystalline or semistable period rings, no Galois action on them and no Tate modules.

targets.target: Conductors of abelian varieties via Artin/Swan conductors (R01)
targets.note: The only conductors are those of Dirichlet characters and the ring-theoretic conductor; grep artinConductor/swanConductor is empty. Higher ramification groups exist only for places of function fields (Tau Ceti).

targets.target: Preservation of good reduction under isogeny
targets.note: Isogenies of abelian varieties exist over a field, and isogenies of group schemes over any affine base (Tau Ceti, with base change), but there are no abelian schemes and no transfer of good reduction.

targets.target: Local Euler polynomial from monodromy and component data, not just the semisimplified inertia action
targets.note: Mathlib defines the local polynomial of an elliptic curve by reduction type (1 − aT + qT², 1 − T, 1 + T, 1) and the resulting L-function; no Galois-theoretic definition or comparison exists.

duplicates.note: States Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich for elliptic curves (good reduction ⇔ unramified T_ℓ) in three separate statements.
Constructs Tate modules of elliptic curves and abelian varieties with the good-reduction Frobenius polynomial, isogeny compatibility and the local Euler-polynomial interface.
Defines Artin/Swan conductors and gives the precise comparison with the conductor of an elliptic curve.
Deduces the good-reduction crystalline and semistable-reduction semistable statements for Tate modules.

targets.target: Character-group exact sequences and monodromy maps with degeneracy-map functoriality, supplied to level lowering
targets.note: An export of R11.2/R11.4 objects, none of which exists.

targets.target: Semistable and good-reduction facts supplied to R25 and to the isogeny-height analysis of R28
targets.note: Interface over R11.3/R11.5, which are unbuilt.

targets.target: Equation-level versus scheme-level comparison for every elliptic invariant used in R29 (minimal discriminant, reduction type, conductor exponent, component group, minimal differential)
targets.note: The equation-level side exists (minimal models, reduction types, local L-polynomial, a unit-c₄ minimality criterion, and invariance of v(Δ) and of split multiplicative reduction across minimal models); the scheme-level Néron invariants and every comparison are absent.

duplicates.note: Supplies the conductor comparison and local Euler-polynomial interface consumed by R29, the same elliptic-invariant interface.
Builds the equation-level invariants (minimal discriminant, Kodaira symbols, Ogg exponent, c_p) that this layer compares with Néron-model data.

PELModuli.summary: No PEL layer is built: neither library has abelian schemes, polarisations of abelian varieties, Rosati involutions, Tate modules, level structures, quasi-isogenies, algebraic spaces or stacks, deformation theory of abelian schemes, higher-dimensional complex tori, analytification, H¹(ℚ, G) for algebraic groups, complex multiplication or canonical models. The libraries supply the linear algebra and generic foundations: Mathlib's star rings, Wedderburn–Artin, adjoint pairs and alternating forms, dual lattices, characteristic polynomials with base change, real signatures, formal smoothness and smooth morphisms of relative dimension n, abstract descent data and stacks, and relative normalisation; Tau Ceti's Sp_{2m} and form-preserving group schemes over any ring (isometries, not similitudes), compatible complex structures with positivity, polarised weight-one Hodge structures, Smith normal forms of integer matrices, local equivalence of quadratic forms over number fields, and abelian varieties over a field with endomorphism rings and isogenies. Genuinely missing are the PEL datum itself, similitude groups, the Kottwitz determinant condition and reflex field, and every moduli-theoretic construction and comparison.

targets.target: Integral, rational and p-integral PEL data (order in a semisimple ℚ-algebra with positive involution, lattice with 𝒪-action, alternating pairing with ⟨bx, y⟩ = ⟨x, b*y⟩, compatible h with positivity) with restriction and rationalisation maps
targets.note: The separate ingredients are in Mathlib (adjoint pairs of bilinear forms, alternating forms, involutive star rings, Wedderburn–Artin, lattices), but there are no orders in noncommutative algebras, no positivity condition tr(bb*) > 0 for involutions, and no PEL datum (grep PEL / positive involution empty).

targets.target: Similitude group (GSp/GU) of the pairing with its multiplier character and representation
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Sp_{2m} for the standard form and the closed subgroup scheme of GL_n preserving a constant form over any commutative ring — isometry groups, multiplier one — plus a rank-2 lemma that the multiplier of AᵀJA = dJ is det A. No declaration mentions GSp or similitudes ('similitude' occurs only in a metric-space docstring).

targets.target: Dual lattice, discriminant and bad-prime set of the pairing
targets.note: The dual lattice of any (including alternating) bilinear form and double duality are available; discriminant groups and unimodularity exist only for symmetric integral lattices. No discriminant or bad-prime set for alternating 𝒪-lattices.

targets.target: Real signature data
targets.note: Signatures and Sylvester classification exist for real quadratic forms; signatures (p, q) of hermitian forms at the complex places of a CM field do not.

targets.target: Positivity condition related to the associated (polarised weight-one) Hodge structure
targets.note: Tau Ceti has compatibility of a complex structure J with a symplectic form (J-invariance and positivity of ω(v, Jv)), the weight-one Hodge structure of J, and the Riemann relations implying a polarisation; the 𝒪-linear version is absent.

targets.target: Determinant condition via characteristic polynomials of the 𝒪-action on the Hodge subspace V₀, equivalent to the representation-theoretic condition over a splitting field
targets.note: Mathlib has the generic characteristic polynomial of a linear family with base change, and Tau Ceti splits V ⊗ ℂ into the ±i eigenspaces of J; no Kottwitz condition (grep empty), and no Brauer–Nesbitt-type comparison in arbitrary characteristic.

targets.target: Reflex field of the determinant condition, identified with D3's reflex field when the datum is Shimura
targets.note: No reflex field in either library ('reflex' occurs only in 'reflexive' and 'reflexion', and 'reflex field' has no hits). The cited splitting-field descent for central simple algebras is a distant ingredient.

duplicates.note: Verifies the determinant condition for the Hilbert–Blumenthal problem, the real-multiplication case of the PEL linear algebra.

targets.target: Fibred categories of polarised abelian schemes with 𝒪-endomorphisms, Rosati compatibility, determinant condition and level structure
targets.note: No abelian schemes, polarisations of abelian varieties, dual abelian varieties or Rosati involutions (the only polarisations are those of Hodge structures, in Tau Ceti). Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field with their endomorphism rings, and Mathlib has fibred categories.

targets.target: Prime-to-p level structures as the étale sheaf of trivialisations of the prime-to-p Tate module, and the all-primes adelic variant in characteristic zero
targets.note: No Tate modules or level structures. Mathlib has the small étale site of a scheme, on which such a sheaf of trivialisations would live, and the finite adeles; Tau Ceti has only affine fppf torsors G → G/H.

targets.target: Isomorphism, rational quasi-isogeny and prime-to-p quasi-isogeny moduli problems and their comparison under changes of lattice and polarisation type
targets.note: grep quasi-isogeny is empty. Isogenies exist between abelian varieties over a field, between affine group schemes over any commutative ring and between elliptic curves over a field, but there is no quasi-isogeny data and nothing over a base for abelian varieties.

targets.target: Effective descent for objects and morphisms of the moduli problems, without assuming the functor of isomorphism classes is a sheaf
targets.note: Mathlib has descent data and the stack condition for pseudofunctors, comonadicity of extension of scalars along faithfully flat maps, fpqc descent of morphism properties, and subcanonicity of the fpqc and fppf topologies (morphisms of schemes descend; the instance is anonymous and cited by Lean's generated name); no stack instance is proved for any concrete moduli pseudofunctor and there is no effective descent of schemes.

targets.target: Principal level structure with the pairing constraint and its multiplier/trivialisation at non-self-dual lattices
targets.note: No Weil pairing; only the rank-2 linear-algebra fact that an alternating form scaled by d under φ has det φ = d.

duplicates.note: Constructs the Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli problem with polarisation modules and level structures, the real-multiplication instance of these functors.

targets.target: Artin-type representability criterion: algebraic Isom functors, finite presentation and limits, deformation/obstruction theory, effectivity, openness
targets.note: Mathlib proves Zariski-local representability of sheaves by schemes and the limit property of locally finitely presented morphisms; there are no algebraic spaces or stacks and no Artin criteria (grep empty).

targets.target: Rigidity: a sufficiently rigidifying prime-to-p level kills automorphisms
targets.note: Only a Serre-lemma-type statement for roots of unity in a domain and Aut(E) ≅ ℤ/2 for elliptic curves with j ∉ {0, 1728}.

targets.target: Representing algebraic space with universal abelian scheme, and the stack formulation at levels with stabilisers
targets.note: The only universal object is the universal Weierstrass curve over ℤ[a₁, …, a₆], not a moduli family.

targets.target: Good-prime hypotheses: unramified order, invertible discriminant/polarisation defect, p = 2 quaternionic exclusion, no level at p
targets.note: Unramified primes are defined for commutative algebras (Mathlib), with the discriminant criterion for number fields; there are no orders in noncommutative semisimple algebras, no polarisation-defect or quaternionic conditions and no level at p.

targets.target: Smoothness from the deformation calculation, relative dimension formula and base change
targets.note: The infinitesimal lifting criterion and smooth morphisms of relative dimension n (stable under base change) are in Mathlib, as are divided-power structures, the thickening input to Grothendieck–Messing; Serre–Tate/Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory of abelian schemes is absent (grep empty).

duplicates.note: Verifies the representability hypotheses for the Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli problem, a special case of this layer.

targets.target: Complex uniformisation morphism with its family and level data (polarised complex tori ℂ^g/Λ with Riemann forms)
targets.note: Only genus-one analytic objects exist: rank-2 period lattices with ℘ and the Jacobi theta functions. Mathlib has ℤ-lattices in real spaces of any dimension and Tau Ceti the linear-algebra Riemann relations, but there are no complex tori ℂ^g/Λ, no Riemann theta functions of genus g and no Siegel space.

targets.target: Analytification of étale presentations, algebraisation of the analytic component isomorphism and descent (scheme/quasi-projectivity in characteristic zero)
targets.note: No analytification, GAGA or algebraisation of analytic maps (grep analytification/GAGA is empty; 'algebraiz' hits only Mathlib's `algebraize` tactic).

targets.target: Image in the PEL moduli space by rational isomorphism classes of polarised representations; open-and-closed Shimura components and the disjoint-union statement
targets.note: Neither PEL moduli spaces nor Shimura varieties exist.

targets.target: Indexing of rational forms by ker¹(ℚ, G) with the Hasse principle deciding single components
targets.note: Mathlib has nonabelian H¹ of a presheaf of groups on a family of objects and Tau Ceti has continuous H¹ with abelian coefficients; no H¹(ℚ, G) for algebraic groups, ker¹ or Hasse principle (grep empty). Tau Ceti defines local equivalence of quadratic forms over a number field (the hypothesis side of Hasse–Minkowski, i.e. of ker¹ for orthogonal groups), but proves no Hasse principle.

targets.target: Disconnected type-D similitude groups and comparison of the moduli problem with the identity component
targets.note: Orthogonal and special orthogonal group schemes for the standard form, abstract orthogonal groups, geometric connectedness of SO_n (char ≠ 2) and the general identity-component and component-group machinery exist; O_n° = SO_n and π₀(O_n) = ℤ/2 are not stated, and there is no GO/GSO and no moduli comparison.

duplicates.note: Proves complex uniformisation with polarisation and level, constructs the Siegel universal analytic family and compares level structures with symplectic lattice trivialisations.
Finishes the algebraisation of polarised weight-one variations over smooth algebraic bases using M3 and Borel algebraicity.
Compares the complex fibres of the Hilbert–Blumenthal problem with the adelic descriptions.

targets.target: Compatibility of the moduli Galois action with CM reciprocity and identification of generic-fibre pieces with canonical models
targets.note: No complex multiplication, Shimura reciprocity or canonical models (grep canonical model finds only concrete quadratic number fields).

targets.target: Compatibility of these identifications with changes of level, isogenies and morphisms of PEL data
targets.note: No moduli spaces or canonical models to compare.

targets.target: Normal integral model at higher p-level as the normalisation of the good-level model in the generic-fibre cover
targets.note: Mathlib has the relative normalisation of a qcqs morphism with its universal property and compatibility with smooth base change — the construction used here — but no good-level model or generic-fibre cover to apply it to.

targets.target: Finiteness, normality and flatness of these normalisations under their actual hypotheses
targets.note: Finiteness of integral closure is known for separable extensions of integrally closed Noetherian domains (Mathlib); Tau Ceti adds the purely inseparable case over a polynomial ring (Stacks 032O) and Krull–Akizuki; there are no Nagata/excellent rings and no normal-scheme predicate, so finiteness over ℤ_(p)-schemes is unavailable.

duplicates.note: Applies the main theorem of complex multiplication to the Siegel moduli model to show its Galois action satisfies the canonical-model condition.

targets.target: Siegel moduli for every dimension g
targets.note: No moduli of principally polarised abelian varieties ('Siegel' occurs only for Siegel's lemma, the Thue–Siegel–Roth theorem, a citation and a TODO on algebraic dependence).

targets.target: Genus-one comparison with #81, including its determinant/Weil-pairing convention
targets.note: Elliptic Weierstrass curves over rings and their classification by j over separably closed fields exist, but they are not linked to abelian varieties, #81 is unformalised and there is no Weil pairing. Genus-one torsion inputs exist (#ker[n] = n² over an algebraically closed field).

targets.target: Trace-pairing PEL datum for a totally real field and a polarisation module (handed to H1–H2)
targets.note: Totally real fields, the trace form, trace duals (the different), totally positive elements (the positivity cone of a polarisation module) and narrow class groups exist; no PEL datum.

targets.target: Unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures, verifying positivity, reflex field, dimension and good-prime conditions
targets.note: Only CM fields and abstract unitary matrix groups; no hermitian forms with signatures or unitary group schemes.

targets.target: At least one non-principal polarisation type
targets.note: No polarisations of abelian varieties and no non-principal example. Tau Ceti has polarisations of Hodge structures with a not necessarily unimodular form, and Smith normal forms of nonsingular integer matrices, which give the type (d₁ | d₂ | …) of a form; Mathlib has dual lattices.

duplicates.note: Proves, for genus one, agreement of the Siegel family with #81's elliptic scheme, differential and pairing — the same genus-one comparison.
Constructs all Siegel data and the Hilbert trace-pairing symplectic embedding at the level of Shimura data.
Builds the Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli problem from polarisation modules, the example M5 hands over.

targets.target: Moduli stack at arbitrary level and fine scheme/algebraic space at each rigidifying level, with universal abelian scheme and Hodge line bundle
targets.note: Ingredients only: the abstract stack condition, invertible sheaves, e*Ω for affine groups, the tangent space at the identity of an abelian variety over a field and top exterior powers of free modules; no moduli stacks, universal families or Hodge line bundle (grep empty).

targets.target: Comparison of isomorphism classes with rational moduli points via the descent obstruction (a rational coarse point need not carry a rational family)
targets.note: Only genus-one phenomena: every j in a field is the j-invariant of a curve over that field (Mathlib); for j ∉ {0, 1728} a quadratic twist has the same j but is not isomorphic over the base, and a curve that becomes isomorphic to E over a quadratic L is E or its twist (Tau Ceti), with Galois descent of changes of variables along quadratic extensions. The j-line is not a coarse moduli space and there is no general descent obstruction.

targets.target: Export of the rational-family comparison to height finiteness (R28.1) and of the universal Hodge line (R35.5)
targets.note: Interface over the targets above, which do not exist; Northcott finiteness for heights of number-field points is available.

targets.target: Explicit nonempty Siegel and unitary examples with a nonprincipal polarisation
targets.note: No moduli spaces to be nonempty.

duplicates.note: Proves the descent and level-structure arguments converting moduli points into isomorphism classes, the same comparison it consumes from M6.

ShimuraCompactifications.summary: No toroidal or minimal compactification, Shimura variety, abelian scheme or degeneration theory exists in either library, so every layer except the combinatorial and Hodge-theoretic parts of C0 and C1 is unbuilt. Tau Ceti already has the finite-fan combinatorics of C0 (toric cones and faces, finite fans with support, completeness, subdivisions, regular cones and fan morphisms), complex points of affine monoid algebras and split tori over any ring, and the linear-algebraic mixed Hodge structures with Deligne splitting and strictness needed in C1, together with dynamic parabolics and Levi decompositions on points, unipotent radicals and centres. The GL₂ cases of several targets are in Mathlib: cusps of arithmetic groups are ℙ¹(ℚ), the level-one ring of modular forms is ℂ[E₄, E₆], and level-one cusp forms are the ideal (Δ). Genuinely missing are infinite arithmetic fans with group actions, general toric schemes and torus embeddings over a base, rational boundary components and mixed Shimura data in general, analytic gluing, normal-crossings and projectivity results, semi-abelian degenerations (Tate curve, biextensions, Mumford–Faltings–Chai), integral PEL and Hilbert compactifications, Hodge-line positivity and the Koecher principle.

targets.target: Rational polyhedral cones and their faces
targets.note: Tau Ceti's toric cones are finitely generated, lattice-rational, salient real cones for an integral lattice N → V; Mathlib has faces of pointed cones with their lattice, and Tau Ceti proves a finitely generated cone has finitely many faces and faces of toric cones are toric. The description of faces as σ ∩ u⊥ is not stated.

targets.target: Fan axioms: closure under faces, pairwise intersections are common faces
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `Fan` has these axioms but requires finitely many cones (a structure field), so it cannot express the infinite arithmetic fans needed here.

targets.target: Arithmetic-admissible collections: arithmetic group action with finitely many orbits, local finiteness in the domain of positivity, support and compatibility conditions at cusps
targets.note: Only generic actions exist: linear maps act on pointed cones pointwise (Mathlib), and the units of a number field act on its mixed space with the fundamental cone as a fundamental domain modulo torsion. No arithmetic group acts on a fan, there is no finiteness of cones modulo a group, and local finiteness exists only as the generic topological notion.

targets.target: Common refinements and sufficiently fine smooth/projective refinements
targets.note: The subdivision relation (a preorder, inducing a fan morphism) and regularity of cones/fans are defined; existence of common, smooth or projective refinements is absent, as are strictly convex support functions, and regular cones are not yet shown simplicial (Mathlib defines simplicial cones).

targets.target: Compatibility with rational parabolic inclusions and level changes
targets.note: No boundary components or parabolics attached to cones.

targets.target: Affine toric charts over the base rings of integral models
targets.note: Only the ℂ-points of Spec ℂ[S] for a monoid S, with an embedding-independent topology and a closed embedding into ℂʳ, exist; monoid algebras and their finite type are in Mathlib. The dual cone σ^∨ is in Mathlib, but its lattice points σ^∨ ∩ M and Gordan's lemma are not. The chart of the zero cone, the split torus Spec R[M], exists over any commutative ring (Tau Ceti), and affine space over any base is in Mathlib, but neither is presented as a toric chart, and there is no affine toric scheme U_σ in general.

targets.target: Gluing of toric charts and torus embeddings relative to a torus torsor by descent
targets.note: Mathlib's scheme gluing is never applied to fans (only the complex points of affine toric varieties exist, and nothing is glued), and scheme torsors exist only as the affine fppf quotient square; grep torus embedding is empty.

targets.target: Properness from the support criterion under the established fan hypotheses
targets.note: Completeness of a finite fan and the valuative criterion exist; no toric variety to apply them to.

duplicates.note: Defines toric cones, rays, regular cones, finite fans, subdivisions, fan morphisms, dual semigroups and affine toric schemes — the finite-fan version of C0's cone, fan and chart targets.
Proves properness of toric maps by the support criterion for finite fans.

targets.target: Rational boundary components (from V2) of Hermitian symmetric domains
targets.note: Only the GL₂ case: cusps of subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) as parabolic fixed points; for arithmetic subgroups they are exactly ℙ¹(ℚ), the rational boundary points of ℍ, with finitely many orbits. No Hermitian domains or boundary components in general.

targets.target: Associated rational parabolic subgroups, unipotent radicals and their centres, Levi quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has dynamic parabolics P(λ) with the Levi decomposition U(λ) ⋊ Z(λ) ≃ P(λ) on points, unipotent radicals and centres of affine groups over a field, and, for GL_N only, scheme-level weight parabolics with their Levi decomposition and unipotent radical (`weightParabolicSemidirectProductCoordinateIso`). There is no GSp or Siegel parabolic, no classification of ℚ-parabolics, and the centre of a unipotent radical and its character lattice are never specialised.

targets.target: Cones of positivity attached to boundary components
targets.note: Positive-definite matrices, real symmetric (Tau Ceti's open set) or Hermitian over any partially ordered star ring (Mathlib's `PosDef`, closed under sums and invariant under congruence by invertible matrices), are not packaged as a cone attached to a boundary component, and there are no general self-dual homogeneous cones.

targets.target: Mixed Hodge structures with weight filtration
targets.note: Linear-algebraic mixed Hodge structures (rational weight filtration, Hodge filtration, pure graded pieces), Deligne's splitting I^{p,q} and strictness of morphisms. Not in Deligne-torus form and with no variations.

targets.target: Mixed Shimura data at the boundary
targets.note: grep mixed Shimura is empty; pure Shimura data are also absent.

targets.target: Pure quotient of a boundary component and the torus and abelian torsors describing its neighbourhood
targets.note: No boundary components and no torsors over boundary strata.

targets.target: Incidence and conjugation formulas, cusp labels and stabilisers
targets.note: Only for GL₂: the translation part of the stabiliser of ∞, cusp widths (at every cusp orbit of a finite-index subgroup, Tau Ceti), the conjugation formula for cusps and cusp orbits as coset classes (Mathlib). No cusp labels in the PEL or general sense.

duplicates.note: Constructs the rational boundary components and their incidence as part of the Baily–Borel construction, the components C1 enriches.
Owns mixed Hodge structures and Deligne's strictness, the mixed Hodge structure C1 needs; built in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Local partial compactifications from relative torus embeddings, their transition and separation properties, arithmetic quotient charts and gluing
targets.note: No complex analytic spaces or analytic gluing; Tau Ceti has biholomorphic mixed monomial chart changes and Mathlib topological gluing and proper discontinuity for arithmetic subgroups of GL₂. Mathlib extends a periodic holomorphic function bounded at ∞ holomorphically across q = 0, the function-level shadow of the one-dimensional torus embedding ℂˣ ⊂ ℂ.

targets.target: Normality, properness and open immersion of the Shimura variety
targets.note: Only the generic morphism classes and relative normalisation; no Shimura varieties and no normal-scheme predicate.

targets.target: Normal-crossings boundary at neat level for smooth fans; projectivity for projective admissible fans
targets.note: Cartier divisors and Proj exist (the latter unindexed because of «» quoting), and Proj of a finitely generated graded algebra is proper over its degree-zero part (an anonymous instance, cited by Lean's generated name); there are no normal crossings, ample line bundles or projective-morphism predicate.

targets.target: Map to the minimal compactification and inverse images of boundary strata
targets.note: grep Baily/Satake/minimal compactification finds nothing.

targets.target: Canonical model of the toroidal compactification over the reflex field via boundary canonical models and descent
targets.note: Mathlib has abstract descent data and the stack condition, faithfully flat descent for modules and fpqc descent of morphism properties; Tau Ceti has Galois descent of tori. There are no canonical models and no descent of glued or projective schemes.

ShimuraData.summary: Neither library defines Shimura data or any of their ingredients beyond linear algebra and the GL₂ case: there is no Weil restriction, Deligne torus, Cartan involution, Hermitian symmetric domain in general, variation of Hodge structure, compact dual, reflex field, special point, Hodge/abelian type, neat level, GSp or Siegel/Hilbert datum. What exists is substantial but lower-level: Tau Ceti's linear-algebraic pure and mixed Hodge structures (opposed filtrations ≃ decompositions, Weil operator i^{p−q}, Tate twists, tensor/dual/internal Hom, weight-one structures from complex structures), which already build the Hodge-structure half of D1; Tau Ceti's affine algebraic groups over a field (tori with Galois-equivariant character lattices and Galois descent, reductive/adjoint/derived groups, central isogenies, dynamic parabolics and Levi decompositions on points, Sp_{2m}, rigid monoidal representation categories); Mathlib's adele ring and idele group; and the GL₂ case: arithmetic subgroups, ℍ as a complex manifold with a transitive, proper, holomorphic and isometric SL₂(ℝ)-action, and the effective action of PSL₂(ℤ). The Deligne torus and its representations, the real-group and Hermitian-domain theory, and all datum-level definitions and examples are genuinely missing.

targets.target: Weil restriction Res_{L/K} of affine group schemes by its functor-of-points universal property, with products, group operations and base change
targets.note: Tau Ceti has base change of affine groups with its points adjunction, products and the points functor, and a forgetful restriction-of-scalars functor on commutative algebras; nothing represents A ↦ G(A ⊗_K L). grep for 'Weil restriction' is empty, and 'restriction of scalars' finds only other notions (modules, algebras, sheaves of modules, partial linear maps, Galois groups, root data, and points of a base-changed group).

targets.target: The Deligne torus and the Hilbert groups Res_{F/ℚ} GL₂ as Weil restrictions, with their datum morphisms
targets.note: Tau Ceti can descend the split torus D(M) along a finite Galois extension from a Galois lattice (which with L = ℂ, k = ℝ, M = ℤ² and the swap would give S) and proves SO₂ is a torus, but neither S nor any Hilbert group is instantiated. On points, Tau Ceti embeds Eˣ into GL₂(F) for any quadratic extension E/F with determinant the norm (`GL2NonSplitTorusHom`), which at ℂ/ℝ is S(ℝ) ⊂ GL₂(ℝ), but only as abstract groups.

targets.target: Topological groups of real, p-adic and adelic points G(ℝ), G(ℚ_p), G(𝔸) of an affine algebraic group
targets.note: Mathlib has the adele ring with its topology, G_m(𝔸) as the idele group and topological SL_n/GL_n over topological rings; Tau Ceti proves K is discrete in 𝔸_K. Missing: a topology on the points of a general affine group and the restricted-product topology on G(𝔸_f). Mathlib describes the units of a restricted product algebraically (`RestrictedProduct.unitsEquiv`), which gives G_m(𝔸_f) as a restricted product of groups but no topology for general G.

targets.target: Point comparisons for restriction of scalars: (Res_{L/K} G)(𝔸_K) ≅ G(𝔸_L) and the real points of the Hilbert groups
targets.note: Neither Weil restriction nor the base change 𝔸_L ≅ L ⊗_K 𝔸_K of adele rings exists. Mathlib identifies the infinite adeles of a number field with ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂}, the ring-level input for the real points of the Hilbert groups, but not F ⊗_ℚ ℝ or 𝔸_L with L ⊗_K 𝔸_K.

targets.target: Real analytic Lie group structure on G(ℝ)
targets.note: Mathlib has the (analytic) Lie group class and makes units of complete normed algebras, hence GL_n(ℝ), Lie groups, and the circle group U(1) = SO(2)(ℝ) is an analytic Lie group through the sphere's charts (the instance is anonymous; its name is Lean's generated one). Tau Ceti is building towards the closed-subgroup theorem, which is not yet proved, so a general G(ℝ) gets no Lie group structure.

With ℂ/ℝ, M = ℤ² and the swap this is X*(S), but S is never instantiated.

A finite direct sum of pure structures of several weights has no dedicated object.

targets.note: Tensor products, duals and Tate twists exist on the Hodge side, and the finite-dimensional representations of an affine group over a field form a symmetric rigid monoidal category (Tau Ceti); no character-twist operation on representations and no compatibility of the operations under an equivalence with S-representations exist.

targets.target: Stabiliser of h, tangent quotient and the invariant complex structure from the adjoint Hodge decomposition, with integrability from the bracket relations
targets.note: Smooth almost complex structures exist without any integrability theorem (grep Newlander/Nijenhuis is empty). There is no tangent quotient and no complex structure from an adjoint Hodge decomposition.

targets.target: Homogeneous-space charts, Hausdorffness and second countability of X = G(ℝ)/K_h

There is no manifold structure on G/K (no closed-subgroup theorem; charts only for free properly discontinuous quotients).

targets.target: Hermitian symmetric-domain structure on each connected component, allowing compact real factors of ℚ-simple groups
targets.note: Only ℍ, the GL₂ case, is present: it is a complex manifold with the hyperbolic metric, SL₂(ℝ) acts transitively, properly, holomorphically and isometrically, the stabiliser of i is given in matrix form (for det > 0, g·i = i iff a = d and b = −c), and ℍ is identified with the disc. Stab(i) = SO(2) and SL₂(ℝ)/SO(2) ≃ ℍ are not stated (both are short compositions), and there is no notion of Hermitian symmetric domain and no general symmetric domain. The anonymous instances carry Lean's generated names.

review.notes: Reviewed all 213 targets of the five roadmaps (48 layers). Mechanical checks: all 48 batch layers are present; the 77 duplicate ids are live atlas stages, none retired or self-referential; every verdict agrees with its targets' statuses. The audit's 349 citations (268 distinct declarations in 213 files) all match declarations.tsv at the stated library, file and line except three declarations the index omits (the anonymous instances `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.instAddCommGroup` and `UpperHalfPlane.instContractibleSpace`, and `«Proj»`). Lean check: in a Tau Ceti build pinned to the same Mathlib, 196 of the 213 cited files are byte-identical and built, but eight of those modules have sources newer than their .olean, so their names were checked at source; all other names resolve in Lean with axioms only among propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, except `HeckeRing.GL2.commRingHeckeRingGamma0`, which is private (cited at R14.1 T3 and R14.2 T3). It is replaced by the public `commSemiringHeckeRingGamma0` and the multiplication-table theorem. No cited file contains sorry, and nothing cited is an axiom. After the corrections there are 454 citations of 351 distinct declarations: 303 were re-checked in Lean (all public, undeprecated, at the stated line, standard axioms) and 48 at source; anonymous instances are cited by their Lean-generated names. Presence claims: R12.4 T1 holds (Lean finds `ConnectedSpace` for the orbit space of Γ(N) on ℍ by instance search; the contractibility instance is at line 68, not 67), as do C0 T1, C1 T4 and D1 T3; the four partly built verdicts and the process verdict for R13.4, which the roadmap defines as the combination of R13.4a and R13.4b, are confirmed. Absences: every absent or partial target was re-searched independently, by concept and Mathlib naming convention, over both trees and the index, and every reported hit was read at source before use. All layer verdicts stand, but seven targets move from absent to partial: R12.1 T4 (the SL₂(ℤ) transformation of Eisenstein summands, i.e. homothety for ℤz + ℤ), R13.3 T2 (Tau Ceti's widths at every cusp), C1 T1 (cusps of arithmetic groups are ℙ¹(ℚ)), C4 T1 (split tori with their characters over any ring), C5 T2 (the level-one graded ring ℂ[E₄, E₆]), C6 T6 (level-one cusp forms are the ideal (Δ)) and D2 T5 (ℍ as a complex manifold with a transitive, proper, isometric SL₂(ℝ)-action). In four of these the audit had itself labelled its citations 'special case'. Thirty-nine notes asserted a non-existence or restriction that is false; the substance of the status survives in each. The recurring one is that group schemes and isogenies exist only over a field: Mathlib's `hopfSpec` and Tau Ceti's `ClosedSubgroupScheme` and `GroupScheme.IsIsogeny` work over an affine or arbitrary base. Others: no Picard functor, no polarisations, no theta functions, no Lie group structure on any closed subgroup (the circle is one), no group action on cones, no descent of varieties, widths only at ∞, and no stabiliser-of-filtration description of GL_N parabolics. Eight literal grep claims were reworded (reflex, similitude, Siegel, algebraiz, IsExcellent, Weil restriction, special point; HeckeAlgebra with the private-citation fix). Two fit labels changed from 'special case' to 'related' (M0 T2, C2 T1), two overstated generalities were corrected (the identity component needs an algebraically closed field; the cited quotient homeomorphism needs a compact quotient), and forty entries gained relevant citations. Duplicates: all 77 claims were checked against the target layers' text and hold; the §5C note no longer says 'word for word'; three overlaps were added (R11.3 ↔ C4 for the Raynaud extension and degeneration data, R13.5 → R15.3 for Igusa curves). The five roadmap summaries were brought in line with the corrected entries.
